llm.summary: This Hex connector skill is coherent, but it needs review because its fallback setup tells agents to install the OOMOL CLI by executing a remote script directly.

dimensions.detail: Bash access is scoped to oo commands in metadata, and OOMOL is described as injecting Hex credentials server-side, but the connected account can still read Hex project data and trigger or cancel runs.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The first-time setup section includes curl-to-bash and PowerShell iex installer commands for the oo CLI without checksum, signature, version pinning, or explicit user approval before running the installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill tells agents to fetch live action schemas before sending payloads and explicitly requires user confirmation for write and destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses one-time CLI installation, OOMOL sign-in, and Hex connection setup; these create persistent local/account state but no hidden background service or backdoor is present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose is to operate Hex through an OOMOL-connected account, and the listed actions fit that purpose, including reads plus run_project and cancel_run as state-changing operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust OOMOL and are comfortable connecting it to Hex. Avoid letting an agent run the remote installer automatically; prefer reviewing the official install instructions, using a pinned release, and verifying integrity before installation. Confirm every run_project or cancel_run action before execution.
llm.findings: [SC2] expected: Confirmed in SKILL.md: installing the required oo CLI is purpose-related, but the documented pipe-to-shell installer executes mutable remote code during normal setup recovery, so this supply-chain concern is accepted as a review issue rather than treated as malicious behavior.
